summary: Madison County, NY 67-foot-6 International Derrick tower built by CCC Camp S-103 in 1940 on Morrow Mountain; closed in 1970 and later removed.

facts.status_note: Closed at the end of the 1970 season and later removed. A New Hartford resident recently bought the dismantled parts and hopes to re-erect the tower at a camp in Oppenheim, NY; the list says only 'recently'. No source describes the summit today.

access.note: Morrow Mountain State Forest is open year-round at no charge. The tower is gone, and no source says what remains on the summit.

events.note: Erected by the CCC Camp S-103, DeRuyter, on Morrow Mountain.
Closed at the end of the 1970 season because aerial detection had taken over; later removed.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLA list calls the site Georgetown Mountain, while the NYSFFLA chapter places the Georgetown tower on Morrow Mountain, 3 1/2 miles north of the village. The story uses both names. The editor may want Morrow Mountain added as another name.

notes_for_editor: The NYSFFLA entry is the only detailed history source; the FFLA list and the DEC forest page confirm the site and its public status. No source we read describes what remains on the summit. An FFLA New York Facebook post about visiting this site and the nearby Morgan Hill site appeared in search, but the page could not be read (fetch returned only its title), so it is not cited and may be worth a browser check. The DEC page does not mention the tower. The sale of the dismantled parts is undated in the source.
